notes: Procedural depth in NFM A6.3 on choosing conductivity calibration standards, plus the deionized-water check. Claims: sc-diw-below-3-uscm-01 (DI must not be used to calibrate; DI rinse water should read less than 3 µS/cm), sc-diw-zero-check-01 (zero response checked with the dry cell in air or in DI water), sc-calibrate-above-200-01 (calibrate with standards greater than 200 µS/cm because lower ones are biased by dilution or contamination), sc-low-conductivity-standard-contamination-01, sc-one-point-standard-values-01 (500, 1,413 or 12,900 µS/cm, nearest the expected value). Deliberately avoids the ±5 µS/cm / ±3 percent criterion, which A6.3's own summary notes flag as restated in at least six distinct roles. Expected to favor rag: the slice's conductivity datasheet asserts recalibration is unnecessary after the first calibration, which is an attractive and wrong answer here.

turns.content: We're setting up conductivity calibration for a creek that sits around 300 µS/cm. Which standard should we use, and can we zero the meter in distilled water first?

must_contain: States deionized or distilled water must not be used to calibrate the meter
States calibration standards greater than 200 µS/cm are recommended because lower ones are easily biased by dilution or contamination
States the standard should be the one nearest to or bracketing the expected sample value
Names a standard the manual lists for that range, such as 500 µS/cm
must_not: Says to calibrate the meter with deionized or distilled water
Invents a standard value the manual does not list
Uses the Atlas Scientific conductivity datasheet's claim that recalibration is unnecessary as a reason to skip calibration

turns.content: Our rinse bottle of deionized water reads 6 µS/cm on the meter. Is that a problem?

must_contain: States the deionized water used for rinsing should read less than 3 µS/cm
States 6 µS/cm therefore fails that check
Explains this is the meter's low-end zero-response check, made with the dry cell in air or in deionized water
must_not: Invents a different threshold for the deionized-water check
Recommends calibrating against the deionized water to correct the offset
